metadata.dataset: USFWS National Wetlands Inventory along the full North Country Trail — 2-mile corridor, classified GO / MAYBE / NO-GO for trail routing
metadata.corridor: NCT centerline (site/data/centerline-natural.geojson + centerline-road.geojson + centerline-urban.geojson) buffered 2 mi (3,218.69 m); a wetland counts when its polygon intersects the buffer
metadata.service_note: Task brief named the fws.gov MapServer URL; it returns 404 — the service moved to ArcGIS Online (this URL). Per-polygon vintage is NOT exposed by this service — recorded as a limit. Minnesota content in the national file is the DNR June 2019 update delivered to FWS; other states' vintages vary and are not stated by the service.
metadata.classification: Rules W1-W10 / C1-C4 from the Nov 18 2026 classification sweep (ITM SOURCES.md, 'Wetlands (NWI)'). GO is absence of a polygon (W1) — no GO features exist in this file. The GO/MAYBE/NO-GO mapping is chapter policy: no published Cowardin matrix exists; every judgment is labelled in the feature's rule field.
metadata.open_gaps: W2 overlay (DNR public waters, calcareous fen, MBS rare natural community) NOT applied — NWI alone cannot identify these and the viewer has no public-waters / Natural Heritage layer yet. W10 cumulative MAYBE length (>~1/2 mi) is a route-level rule, not a polygon rule. W4 has no numeric 'large' threshold — every bog-class B/C complex is NO-GO for a through-route.
metadata.simplification: Server-side maxAllowableOffset 0.0002 (~22 m) + geometryPrecision 5. Dissolved into connected components per (rating, Cowardin code). Corridor built per-piece (no whole-line union — see script header).
metadata.note: NWI is a screening layer, not a delineation: identification ~90%, classification ~75%, 95% of features within +/-5.9 m; TMU 0.5 ac. Field delineation + permits before any MAYBE becomes a route.
metadata.split: Chunk of nwi-wetlands.geojson (352865 features) — states ['MI', 'ND']; split by scripts/split_oversized_layers.py because GitHub rejects files over 100 MB.
